model_annotations.English: Figure 8(c) presents a grouped bar chart titled “Branching Ratio γB,” illustrating how the branching ratio of reasoning graphs varies with the number of shots (0, 1, 2, 3, 4) under two prompting styles: “Instruct” and “Cot” (Chain-of-Thought). The horizontal axis represents the “Number of Shots,” ranging from 0 to 4, while the vertical axis, labeled “γB,” quantifies the branching ratio on a linear scale from 0 to 0.6, with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. For each shot count, two adjacent bars are shown: the left bar (dark blue) corresponds to the “Instruct” style, and the right bar (light blue) to the “Cot” style. At 0 shots, the “Instruct” bar reaches approximately 0.55, while the “Cot” bar is slightly lower at around 0.52. As the number of shots increases, both bars decrease in height: at 1 shot, “Instruct” drops to ~0.48 and “Cot” to ~0.45; at 2 shots, “Instruct” is ~0.42 and “Cot” ~0.40; at 3 shots, “Instruct” is ~0.38 and “Cot” ~0.36; and at 4 shots, “Instruct” is ~0.35 and “Cot” ~0.33. The chart visually demonstrates that the branching ratio declines monotonically with increasing shot count for both prompting styles, with the “Instruct” style consistently exhibiting a higher branching ratio than “Cot” across all shot levels.
